external_entities.name: Shopper
external_entities.description: A shopper who browses the storefront, signs in, and places orders.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders through the storefront API

external_entities.name: card processor
external_entities.description: A third-party payment processor that settles payments and sends payment status webhooks.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

processes.name: storefront API
processes.description: A Node service running on Cloud Run through which shoppers browse and place orders, and which receives payment webhooks.
processes.source_excerpt: the storefront API, a Node service running on Cloud Run

processes.name: order service
processes.description: A Python worker in the core network that processes orders and reads and writes order data.
processes.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network

data_stores.name: orders-db
data_stores.description: A PostgreSQL database containing orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four values.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four live in a PostgreSQL database (orders-db)

data_stores.name: receipt archive
data_stores.description: A Cloud Storage bucket containing receipts for completed orders.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive

data_flows.name: place orders
data_flows.description: Shopper browsing, sign-in, and order submission to the storefront API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders through the storefront API

data_flows.name: submit order
data_flows.description: The storefront API calls the order service when a shopper submits an order.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When a shopper submits an order the storefront API calls the order service over gRPC.

data_flows.name: read and write orders
data_flows.description: The order service reads and writes orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four values in the database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the order service reads and writes with a single application account that has full read/write

data_flows.name: write receipt
data_flows.description: The order service writes a receipt for every completed order to the receipt archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive.
data_flows.authentication: the order service's own service account
data_flows.data_description: Receipt recording which order was written and that the order service wrote it

data_flows.name: settlement webhook
data_flows.description: The card processor sends a payment-settlement webhook to the storefront API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: After they settle a payment they POST a webhook back to the storefront API to tell us the order is paid.
data_flows.notes: Authentication is uncertain: "I would have to check how that callback is authenticated."
data_flows.data_description: Payment settlement status for an order

trust_boundaries.name: core network
trust_boundaries.description: The organisation's core network where the order service runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network

trust_boundaries.name: card processor
trust_boundaries.description: The third-party environment controlled by the card processor.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

assumptions.assumption: The storefront API presents a web interface because shoppers browse it and the API receives a POST webhook.
assumptions.basis: The description says shoppers browse the storefront and identifies a POST webhook back to the storefront API.

assumptions.assumption: The order service presents a non-web interface because callers reach it through gRPC.
assumptions.basis: The storefront API calls the order service over gRPC; gRPC is an RPC service interface rather than a web application interface.

assumptions.assumption: The orders database contains confidential data.
assumptions.basis: It contains shopper addresses, card-last-four values, and business order records.

assumptions.assumption: The receipt archive contains confidential data.
assumptions.basis: It contains receipts recording completed orders and payment-related order records.

assumptions.assumption: The settlement webhook uses HTTP because the description says the card processor POSTs it to the storefront API.
assumptions.basis: The description explicitly uses the HTTP method POST for the callback.
